messages:
marta (PM): Drafting a compact PRD for model selection + fallback strategy. Need quick alignment on launch criteria and prioritized scope. TL;DR: make safe defaults for hosted, dedicated, and private without blocking eng runtime work.

raj (eng): +1. can you list the acceptance criteria we need for v1? I want to scope runtime changes.

sylvie (product): Starting list: 1) deterministic routing decision tree, 2) compatibility mapping between model variants, 3) documented fallback order per tier, 4) metrics & alerts for mismatches.

marta (PM): Good. Also adding: 5) rollback behavior for pinned customers, 6) latency budget per-tier, 7) canary & A/B gating for rollouts.

raj (eng): From infra side, constraints: we only support identical tokenizer/architecture fallbacks without re-tokenization. So we need a compatibility matrix: model -> compatible fallbacks (quantized, fp16, distilled). Example: "redwood-rwkv-13b" -> ["rwkv-13b-8bit", "rwkv-13b-4bit-qk"].

Tom (runtime): Note: KV cache layout differs between some optimized kernels. Fallback that changes kernel/kv-layout will require cache flush and cold-start penalty. That's an acceptance criterion: fallback must not silently break long-context sessions; must either preserve KV or signal client to reconnect.

raj (eng): Edge case: multi-region sticky sessions. If primary region is down and we failover to a different region with a compatible model, we must choose one of two strategies: preserve session affinity and accept latency bump, or re-route to nearest region with degraded model but lower latency. Product decision?

sylvie (product): For v1, prefer preserve correctness for enterprise customers: failover -> same model family variant in another region even if higher latency. For host-tier free/low tier, prefer lowest latency fallback. We should encode this per-customer tier policy.

marta (PM): Add to PRD: policy precedence order = customer pin > SLA tier policy > region preference > cost optimization. Include example policies in spec.

raj (eng): Acceptance tests we need: 
- compatibility matrix unit tests (mapping lookup)
- integration test: simulated region outage -> fallback chosen matches policy
- KV-cache regression test: session continuity or explicit reconnect delivered to client

Tom (runtime): Also add load-shedding rule: if fallback model causes GPU OOM, runtime should degrade to a queued response + client error to avoid noisy neighbor failures. Documented SLO change.

marta (PM): Launch criteria proposal (all must be green):
- PRD approved by Product + Eng + Security
- compatibility matrix published in Console UI
- automated tests passing in CI (compat + failover sim + regressions)
- rollout playbook includes rollback steps and customer notification templates
- observability: per-route fallback metric + alert on >1% fallback rate for 5m

sylvie (product): Prioritization: Phase 1 (launch): core policy engine + UI exposure + enterprise default. Phase 2: advanced cost-aware routing and ML-based routing heuristics. Phase 1 target: 6 weeks.

raj (eng): Implementation notes: policy engine will be a small stateless service with rules config stored in config-store. Runtime will call the policy engine with request context and receive target model variant + region. We'll need a fast cache for lookups.

Tom (runtime): Runtime changes: accept "fallback_reason" codes, support explicit session-reconnect hint, and surface per-request chosen_variant in traces. Add to acceptance criteria.

marta (PM): Customer-driven asks: two customers asked for guaranteed model-family preserving failover across regions (Tier: enterprise). Mark these as top priority and include in acceptance tests and rollout pilot.

raj (eng): Can we get an initial compatibility CSV from model-onboarding team? format: model,variant,tokenizer,kv_layout,notes. That will help generate the matrix and tests.

sylvie (product): I'll reach out to model-ops. Also adding docs requirement: migration notes for customers pinned to immutable version when fallback occurs.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: canary/policy-engine-v0.1 -> infra-test. Status: started. :rocket:

marta (PM): For launch readiness, owners: policy engine (raj), runtime hooks (tom), console + docs (sylvie), tests & QA (eng-qa). I'll compile a checklist and post tomorrow.

raj (eng): Quick question: should fallback order be editable per-route in Console? I prefer yes but start with per-customer tier only.

sylvie (product): Start with per-customer tier + org-level override in Phase 1. Route-level override as Phase 2.

marta (PM): Edge cases to capture in PRD (short bullets):
- tokenizer mismatch -> explicit failure (no silent fallback)
- KV-layout mismatch -> force reconnect with clear error code
- pinned customer + no compatible fallback -> maintain request queue/backpressure and notify SRE + customer
- model variant unavailability during streaming -> fallback policy MAY attempt variant but must support partial-response cancellation semantics

tom (runtime): I'll prototype the reconnect hint header: `X-RW-Session-Reconnect: reason=kv_layout_mismatch; reconnect_after_ms=200`

marta (PM): Great. I'll add all this to the PRD draft and tag owners. goal: PRD review by EOD Friday. Please add any missing acceptance criteria or edge cases here.

raj (eng): Adding: metric names suggestion: `policy.fallback.count`, `policy.fallback.latency_delta.p50`, `policy.fallback.unavailable_variant.count`.

sylvie (product): Add alert thresholds: P1 if `policy.fallback.count` for enterprise routes > 0.1% sustained 10m, P2 for host-tier >1% 10m.

marta (PM): Awesome. Thanks everyone. I'll post PRD link when ready. :spiral_calendar:
